scope: Compact editor settings; presentation, navigation, browser test navigation and documentation only.

comparison.result: All eight default tool pages fit without vertical scrolling at 1440x900. At 1366x768, the default foliage page needs 89 px of scrolling; the other seven fit. Advanced/expanded settings can scroll. Task tabs and context selectors remain outside the scrolling body.

behavior: Task tabs with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End keyboard navigation and ARIA tab relationships.
Compact inline sliders and value fields; context-specific sculpt controls.
Model settings, effects, LODs and asset operations separated from everyday foliage painting.
Expandable advanced settings and individual LOD entries; static tips expand on demand.
Tool tabs, expanded sections, independent page scroll and focused controls survive inspector refreshes.
Tab navigation leaves document and undo history unchanged; selected props reveal their editing page.

browser.retries: Tests were adapted to navigate task tabs and disclosures. Recovery image assertions now poll for the exact original PNG hash. One prop-drag comparison remained intermittent: diagnosis found four pixels differing by one 8-bit color level at a handle edge; the unchanged final assertion passed on a targeted rerun. No renderer changes or image tolerance were introduced.

limits: Targeted Chrome verification only; the full browser suite, full Vitest suite and cross-browser/device matrix were not rerun for this presentation change.
The isolated editor build reused the existing runtime package outputs for browser fixtures. Shared dist/lib and the other agent’s server were not overwritten.
The GPU-dependent exact-image recovery checks have the intermittent single-level color variation described above; a passing rerun is not evidence of deterministic pixels on all hardware.
This does not establish production readiness or measure rendering performance.
